E1.evidence: Maintainer commit 753226d (vooon, 2015-09-17T16:22Z) "extras #387: fix header stamp in joint_states" adds the single line `states->header.stamp = msg->header.stamp;` to `ServoStatePublisher::rc_out_cb` in mavros_extras/src/servo_state_publisher.cpp. At the parent revision ef384ed the callback builds `auto states = boost::make_shared<sensor_msgs::JointState>();`, fills only `states->name` and `states->position`, and calls `joint_states_pub.publish(states);` with the header stamp left at its zero default. Issue #387 ("Make Joint state publisher from rc/out") is the feature request for the node; it has no comments and was closed before the fix. No reproducer or error log is given; the maintainer's fix commit is the confirmation.

E2.evidence: The parent commit ef384ed ("test: new test for local_position + SSP (#387) + URDF", 18 minutes before the fix) adds test_mavros/launch/apm/apm_local_position_test.launch, which starts `<node name="robot_state_publisher" pkg="robot_state_publisher" type="robot_state_publisher" />` and `<node pkg="mavros_extras" type="servo_state_publisher" name="servo_state_publisher">` in the same launch, both under the same `robot_description`. The two nodes are separate processes from separate packages interacting only through the `joint_states` topic (`joint_states_pub = nh.advertise<sensor_msgs::JointState>("joint_states", 10);` in servo_state_publisher.cpp; `joint_state_sub_ = n.subscribe("joint_states", 1, &JointStateListener::callbackJointState, this);` in robot_state_publisher). The defect is a value crossing that boundary: the message's `header.stamp` is sent unset (zero) while the consumer reads it (`if (state->header.stamp >= last_published + publish_interval_)` and `state_publisher_.publishTransforms(joint_positions, state->header.stamp, tf_prefix_);`). A wrong timing value that crosses the boundary is an interface failure even though the resolving edit is inside the provider (step 2 does not stop). Steps 3-5 do not apply: the fix changes the published message content, not names, build, or firmware. Eligible; interface kind: topic.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the servo_state_publisher output (`sensor_msgs/JointState` on `joint_states`) feeds robot_state_publisher's input; both run concurrently in the test launch, but the failing interaction is the data hand-off.

E4.evidence: Code-level statement by the maintainer's commit "extras #387: fix header stamp in joint_states" with the added line `states->header.stamp = msg->header.stamp;` (https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/commit/753226d93a735ba01744620b5654b8a038d1c89d). No observed effect (no log, no rviz observation) is recorded anywhere in the issue or commits, so the outcome class is `undocumented`.

resolution.summary: Provider side: copy the incoming RCOut header stamp into the published JointState, `states->header.stamp = msg->header.stamp;` in ServoStatePublisher::rc_out_cb (mavros_extras/src/servo_state_publisher.cpp, commit 753226d). The consumer is unchanged.
resolution.evidence: The fix is committed to master by the maintainer ("extras #387: fix header stamp in joint_states", https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/commit/753226d93a735ba01744620b5654b8a038d1c89d) but the source never shows the test composition running with it.

notes: Class `other`: the message type and definition match on both sides; the defect is the timing value carried in `header.stamp` (left at the zero default). Inference, not documented in the source: at robot_state_publisher 8235bce the callback publishes only when `state->header.stamp >= last_published + publish_interval_` and stamps the TF transforms with `state->header.stamp`, so a zero stamp would suppress or zero-stamp the joint transforms; the source records no such observation, hence `undocumented`. The upstream composition mavros (rc_io plugin, `/mavros/rc/out`, mavros_msgs/RCOut) -> servo_state_publisher (`<remap from="rc_out" to="/mavros/rc/out" />`) is not a failed interaction; the fix merely forwards its stamp. Both units also read `param:/robot_description` set by the launch file (servo_state_publisher: `model.initParam("robot_description")`), a shared input rather than an element exchanged between the two, so it is not listed in the inventory. Topic name: advertised as relative `joint_states` on a public NodeHandle, i.e. `/joint_states` in the test launch's root namespace. The test launch lives in the `test_mavros` package of the same repository; it wires but does not own either node. The ROS distro is not stated; the repository's .travis.yml at ef384ed still says `ROS_DISTRO=hydro` with a comment "wait until travis will update to 14.04", which is CI configuration rather than a statement about the test.
